results.name: stream-engine-kill
notes: windows published during the outage waited on the SQS ingest queue and were processed on restart; the batch in flight at the kill was redelivered after the visibility timeout (those windows count as late_windows: stored, not applied to live state)
emitted_not_stored compares the engine's store with the archiver's independent copy

results.name: agent-down
notes: the SOS was paged by the rules path while the agent service was stopped; the brief followed once it restarted and drained its queue (SQS retains the events)

results.name: alert-service-kill
notes: the escalation timer came due while the service was down; it fired from Postgres on restart and paged

results.name: archiver-kill
notes: messages are deleted from the archive queue only after their object is written, so the buffer lost in the kill was redelivered and archived after the visibility timeout
archive_duplicates > 0 is expected (at-least-once); readers de-duplicate on msg_id
the real-time path has its own queue: its latency is unaffected by the archive outage
